newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.

text.p: In the South, rice prices were steady. Long grain milled rice prices were selling mostly at $19.50 per cwt, some discounts of up to $1.00 were reported; Medium grain traded mostly at $18.00-19.00; Second heads were steady at $14.00-15.00 and Brewers remain in very tight supply with few quotes at $14.75-15.75. Rice by-products were steady.

In California, rice prices were steady with Medium grain selling mostly at $19.50. Rice bran was steady to $2.00 lower. There were 682,926 cwt of U.S. Medium Grain rice inspected for the week ending Dec 28, 1996. The yearly total since October 1, 1996 is 3,119,105 cwt compared to 2,443,152 cwt a year ago.

California rice ship loadings for the week ending December 28, 1996, at Sacramento the Emmagracht loaded 10,000 mt of US No 1 bagged Medium grain brown rice destined for Japan; the Manyas 1 loaded 10,560 mt of US No. 1 Med grain bulk rough rice and 4,033 mt of US No. 1 med grain milled rice destined for Turkey. At Stockton the MV Tnkerball loaded 10,000 mt of US No 1 bagged Med Grain brown rice destined for Japan.

The following prices were for domestic shipment -- offers, FOB mills, milles rice, dollars per cwt, bagged. (All milled rice grade 2 not to exceed 4 percent brokens, except California grade 1. All second heads grade 4 or better.
Feed by-products prices (dollars per short ton, fob mills).
